newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Tongaat-Hulett sees growth in current year.
newsitem.headline: Tongaat-Hulett sees growth in current year.

text.p: South African sugar to property group Tongaat-Hulett Ltd said on Friday that it expected to post real earnings growth in its current financial year.

"All divisions have forecast real growth in profits for the 1997/98 financial year and this should translate into an increase in real earnings per share at group level," the firm said in a statement with its year results.
Earlier the firm posted earnings per share of 472.3 cents, up from 350.4 cents last time and slap in the midddle of analysts' expectations.
The firm said the current year would be hampered by only modest South African economic growth, but an expected cut in interest rates towards the end of the year would stimulate demand.
It also said it would benefit from a predicted continued decline of the rand against the dollar.

The firm's local sugar operations had a strong year, reaping the benefits of a 56 percent increase in the sugar cane crop. The firm saw its mill tonnage hit 902,000 tons -- the highest level since 1991/92.
Tongaat-Hulett's international sugar interests, predominately its wholly-owned Zimbabwe unit Triangle Sugar Corp Ltd, also had a good year.
Triangle, one of the lowest cost sugar producers in the world, produced 176,000 tons of sugar and is budgetting for 300,000 tons in the current year due to improved water resources.
The firm is also looking at expanding elsewhere in southern Africa.
"The group has a number of attractive opportunities for extending its sugar activities in the low cost Southern African region and these are being actively pursued," the firm said.

In the group's building materials division performance was depressed as a result of high interest rates, while results from the textiles arm were satisfactory after increasing exports and planning for additional weaving capacity.
In the aluminium division operating earnings were maintained due to improved demand and company strategies to reduce import duties.
The firm said its property arm had an excellent year with progress being made on a host of residential, resort, commercial and industrial projects.
